# 03 — Correction

## Definition [HARD CANON]

Correction is the deliberate alteration or removal of a relationship from the present Float. It is one integrated procedure — it does not delete first and repair continuity afterward. See `meta/lexicon` §III for the full technical specification (target relationship, protected invariants, acceptable collateral effects, reintegration route, stability threshold), which remains accurate and is not superseded here.

Correction is **not** simple memory deletion. Memory changes as a side effect because memory is one expression of a relationship, not the whole of it. Correction is **not** automatic, perfect alternative-history generation — Asterion does not fabricate a complete replacement biography every time something is corrected, and correction does not automatically reconcile every downstream consequence.

## Relationships as Braids [HARD CANON — foundational mechanic]

Human relationships are not simple binary edges. They are overlapping braids: two people can be connected through work, friendship, family, sex, shared place, money, care, conflict, shared language, ritual, memory, trauma, obligation, history, and creative collaboration simultaneously. Removing one strand does not always remove the whole person from the other person's reality. But if the removed strand was the structure around which the others were organized, much more may collapse.

**Canonical example (Thomas and Susan):** Susan and Thomas work together for decades. If nearly all of their relationship existed because they worked together, correcting Thomas out of the company may remove most of the relational structure through which Thomas mattered to Susan — she may barely recognize him at all, and instead experience structural absence (see `meta_bloomrot.md` §Structural Absence): a routine expects someone, a joke has no origin, a space seems arranged around a missing participant. But if Susan and Thomas were close, independent friends outside the workplace, that relationship may survive intact even with no recognized shared work history — which is how people discover contradictory gaps in their own shared lives.

## Direct Relational Effect vs. Downstream Consequence [WORKING CANON — deliberately non-rigid]

Direct relational structures are more likely to be altered by a correction. Consequences may survive. Do not make this boundary mathematically exact — whether something is part of the corrected relationship or merely a consequence can be deeply subjective, and the ambiguity is philosophical, not a technical limitation awaiting resolution.

Worked examples:

| Likely directly corrected | Likely survives as consequence |
|---|---|
| Employee record | Cake knife used for birthday cakes |
| Employee badge | Workflow the person invented |
| Memory of person as coworker | A colleague's career choice they inspired |
| | A marriage between two people they introduced |
| | An office arrangement built around their habits |

## Memory After Correction [HARD CANON]

Do not model memory as a collection of discrete files. Memories contain multiple relationships simultaneously, and correction can sever one while leaving others intact within the *same* memory.

**Canonical example (Thomas and his wife):** Thomas remembers coming home furious after work and sitting with his wife at the kitchen table until two in the morning. His employment relationship is corrected; his marriage is not. He may still remember coming home, being angry, the kitchen, his wife's hand, being comforted, and the emotional importance of the night — while the employment-dependent meaning is gone. Who humiliated him, what happened, where he had been, what the argument was about, why the day had mattered — there may be no recognized answer.

He knows he has been corrected. Correction is a known, named social phenomenon in this world (see `meta_world_and_society.md`) — he does not need to believe he is hallucinating or time-traveling. He can understand *some major relational part of my life has been removed*, and this can still devastate him.

## Missing Provenance Is Not a Paradox [HARD CANON]

If `ALICE ↔ MOTHER ↔ JUNE` is corrected, June does not metaphysically require a replacement mother. June exists now; June may simply have no recognized mother. The Float can contain *June exists* and *June has no recognized mother* simultaneously without contradiction, because people in this world are used to forms of missing provenance created by correction.

Working distinction: **humans demand explanations. Institutions demand fields. Reality merely contains June.** People appear, disappear, have missing parents, have missing histories, and live around relational absence. Society has adapted — see `meta_world_and_society.md`. This is directly compatible with the Alis Dane material already drafted in chapter_1 and requires no revision to that scene.

## Correction Debt [HARD CANON]

Correction often solves an immediate local problem while creating downstream relational damage. Follow-up corrections may be required, and each correction can create residue, distress, contradiction, or secondary instability that requires another correction, which creates additional disruption — **correction debt.**

Correction therefore does not restore global coherence. At best it creates a locally acceptable reality, and even local success may require repeated maintenance. Institutions can spend years maintaining the appearance that an earlier correction "worked." This can happen to people, families, workplaces, healthcare wards, public infrastructure, neighborhoods, or administrative systems. At the extreme, entire environments may become correction sinks, where every intervention is solving a problem partly created by an earlier intervention. See `meta_institutions.md` §The Choir's Systemic Error for the institutional-scale version of this loop.

## Coherence vs. Consistency [WORKING CANON — a philosophical distinction, not a rigid rule]

Correction should not be described as restoring global coherence. At best it creates local compatibility, continuity, consistency, or temporary stability. Reality was not fundamentally incoherent before the Choir; the world already had its own relational coherence, and the Choir discovered that coherence could be altered.

- **Consistency**: the sanctioned version fits together enough to function.
- **Coherence**: the relationships genuinely belong to the whole that produced them.

These terms are available to characters — especially in Continuity-division dialogue (see `meta_institutions.md` §Continuity) — as a live philosophical distinction, not as a scoring system the meta applies from outside.
